intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and offer snorkeling opportunities in crystal-clear waters.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, and spices. Join a guided street food tour to sample spanakopita, loukoumades (honey donuts), souvlaki, and fresh Greek yogurt with honey. A true immersion into everyday Athenian food culture.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow lagoon-like waters. The unique color comes from crushed pink shells mixed with white sand. Wade through the warm shallow waters to reach the small island of Elafonissi and enjoy one of the most beautiful natural beaches in the Mediterranean.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna to learn how to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan bruschetta), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and homemade baklava. You'll visit a local market beforehand to pick fresh ingredients and learn about the health secrets of the Mediterranean diet directly from a local chef.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Santorini Caldera Taverna
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset while dining at a cliffside taverna overlooking the volcanic caldera. Enjoy freshly grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea puree), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and local Assyrtiko white wine. This iconic experience combines spectacular scenery with authentic Cycladic cuisine for an unforgettable evening.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus or Metro Line 3 to your connection point toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a 24-hour kiosk or airport food court upon arrival (budget ~€5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport if needed. Buy a transit card for public transport. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since it is a late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time and get oriented with the local surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local village or town on foot. Visit a small open-air market to pick up fresh fruit, olives, and local snacks. Browse the waterfront tavernas and get a feel for local prices and menus for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby waterfront taverna. Try a classic Greek salad (horiatiki) and grilled octopus or souvlaki. Watch the sunset over the sea from the shoreline.

meals.breakfast: Grab a budget breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bakery — fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring) and Greek coffee for ~€3-4
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh fruit, bread, feta, and olives from the local market for a self-assembled picnic (~€5)
meals.dinner: Local taverna near the beach — Greek salad, souvlaki plate, and a local beer (~€12-15)

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation day. Keep it low-key and budget-friendly. Stock up on water and snacks from a local supermarket to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the nearest public beach early (before 10:00) to claim a good spot. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea and snorkel if you brought or can rent gear cheaply. Public beaches in Greece are free — avoid paying for sunbeds by bringing your own towel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local bus to a nearby cove or quieter stretch of coastline. Explore rock formations, crystal-clear water, and enjoy the scenery. Take photos and relax in the sun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore a local neighborhood for dinner. Look for a traditional Greek psistaria (grill house) away from the tourist strip for more authentic and cheaper food.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café (~€3-5)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade picnic from the supermarket — pita bread, tzatziki, tomatoes, cheese (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: Psistaria grill house — mixed grill plate with pita and dips (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and a hat. The sun is intense at 29°C. Early morning swims are the most refreshing before the beach gets crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local archaeological site, ancient ruins, or a hilltop church within reach of the resort area. Many smaller sites have low or no entry fees. Enjoy panoramic views and learn about the local history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a shaded spot in a local plateia (town square) and people-watch over a long Greek coffee (freddo espresso or frappé). Browse any local craft or souvenir shops — look for handmade ceramics, olive oil products, or local honey as budget-friendly mementos.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals for the traditional evening volta (promenade walk) along the waterfront. Find a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) for a shared small-plates dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita from a local bakery with a coffee (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Gyros pita wrap from a local gyradiko — one of Greece's best budget meals (~€3-4)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio — order 3-4 shared meze dishes like taramosalata, saganaki, dolmades, and grilled vegetables (~€12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many archaeological sites offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month. Check ahead for any local cultural events or festivals happening this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or ferry (if available) to a nearby island or coastal town for a day trip. Explore the harbor, fishing boats, and waterfront. Greece's public ferry system is affordable and a great way to see more of the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at a recommended beach at your day-trip destination. Many Greek island beaches have incredibly clear turquoise water. Explore any hilltop villages (chora) with whitewashed houses and blue-domed churches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Relax on the hotel's beachfront. Cook a simple meal in your room if you have kitchen access, or grab cheap street food.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick pastry from a bakery before departure (~€3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a harbourside taverna at your day-trip destination (~€10-13)
meals.dinner: Supermarket provisions or a cheap souvlaki on return (~€5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Check local ferry or bus schedules the night before and book tickets in advance if possible. Bring cash as smaller island kiosks may not accept cards. Carry water and sunscreen for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise swim at the beach — one of the most magical experiences in Greece. After swimming, take a long walk along the coastal path to explore hidden coves and scenic viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove, vineyard, or farm if accessible nearby. Many Greek families offer informal tastings of olive oil, wine, or raki. Alternatively, visit a local fishing port and watch the afternoon catch come in.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own Greek-inspired meal using fresh market ingredients — grilled vegetables, feta, olives, fresh bread, and local wine from the supermarket. Eat on your balcony or the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Fruit salad and Greek yogurt self-prepared or from a local café (~€3-5)
meals.lunch: Fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and olives from the market — a true Greek picnic (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Self-catered Greek feast from supermarket ingredients — total cost ~€8-10 including a bottle of local wine

day_by_day.notes: A self-catered dinner is a great budget hack and a fun way to engage with local produce. Greek supermarkets (like Sklavenitis or AB Vassilopoulos) stock excellent local products at very reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip — treat yourself to a slightly slower morning. Enjoy a long Greek breakfast at a café overlooking the sea. Read, journal, or simply soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (budget ~€10-20/day) to explore the surrounding countryside and coastline at your own pace. Discover hidden beaches, mountain villages, and scenic viewpoints that are off the tourist trail.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop bar or clifftop taverna for sunset drinks — order a local Mythos or Alfa beer or a glass of house wine. Stay for dinner and enjoy the cooler evening air.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek café breakfast — eggs, bread, honey, fruit, and coffee (~€6-8)
meals.lunch: Stop at a village kafeneion (traditional café) for a simple lunch of bread, cheese, and local snacks (~€5-6)
meals.dinner: Rooftop or clifftop taverna — fresh fish of the day with salad and local wine (~€15-18)

day_by_day.notes: Check that your travel insurance covers scooter rental. Always wear a helmet. This is a great way to see more of Greece without expensive tour costs. Petrol is cheap for a day's riding.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fish market or farmers market early in the morning to experience authentic Greek daily life. Chat with vendors, taste samples, and buy fresh produce. Markets typically run from 07:00-13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach reading, swimming, and relaxing. Try snorkeling to explore the underwater world — rent cheap snorkel gear locally if you don't have your own. Look for sea urchins, fish, and starfish in the clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to a nearby neighborhood away from the tourist zone and find a family-run taverna. These spots offer the most authentic food at the lowest prices. Look for a handwritten menu — a sign of freshness and tradition.

meals.breakfast: Fresh produce from the morning market — tomatoes, bread, olives, and cheese (~€4)
meals.lunch: Packed beach picnic from morning market purchases (~€5)
meals.dinner: Family-run taverna — moussaka or pastitsio with a side salad and house wine (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: The further you walk from tourist hotspots, the cheaper and more authentic the food becomes. A good rule of thumb: if the menu has photos and is in 5 languages, keep walking.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike on a local coastal or mountain trail. Greece has excellent hiking paths with stunning views. Many are free and well-marked. Start early before the heat peaks — aim to finish by 11:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off with a long swim at a beach near the end of the hiking trail. Rest in the shade and enjoy the peaceful surroundings away from the crowds. Explore any sea caves or rock arches if accessible safely.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Treat yourself to a traditional Greek dessert at a local zacharoplasteio (patisserie) — try galaktoboureko (custard pastry), baklava, or loukoumades (honey doughnuts). Then find a cheap souvlaki dinner.

meals.breakfast: Energy-boosting breakfast before the hike — peanut butter on toast or a hearty bakery pie (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — energy bars, fruit, nuts, and water from the supermarket (~€4)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki plate with tzatziki, fries, and pita from a local grill (~€8-10) followed by dessert at a patisserie (~€3-4)

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper footwear for hiking. Carry at least 1.5 liters of water per person. Start the hike no later than 08:00 in summer heat. Download an offline trail map via AllTrails or Maps.me before you go.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby traditional Greek village (chorio) on foot. Wander through narrow whitewashed alleyways, visit a small Byzantine church, and admire the local architecture. Many villages have a free local museum or cultural center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a free or low-cost local cultural event, outdoor cinema, or village festival if one is happening. Greek summers are full of local panigiri (religious festivals) with free music, dancing, and food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals for dinner at a panigiri festival if available (food is very cheap and abundant) or find a local ouzeri for ouzo-paired small plates.

meals.breakfast: Village bakery — fresh bread, local honey, and a strong Greek coffee (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Village kafeneion — simple lunch of salad, bread, and local cheese (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Ouzeri — ouzo with a selection of mezedes: grilled sardines, fava, taramosalata, and olives (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings or ask your hotel reception about any upcoming village festivals or cultural events. Panigiri festivals are one of the most authentic Greek experiences and are almost always free to attend.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your favorite beach for a final long morning swim. Try paddleboarding or kayaking — many beaches offer affordable hourly rentals (~€8-12/hour). Explore the coastline from the water for a different perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — focus on local products like olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, or handmade ceramics rather than mass-produced tourist items. These are better quality and often cheaper.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate a wonderful trip. Choose a well-reviewed local seafood restaurant and try fresh grilled sea bream (tsipoura) or sea bass (lavraki) with lemon and olive oil.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey, walnuts, and fresh figs from the market (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — pita with hummus, olives, and fresh tomatoes from the supermarket (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Seafood taverna splurge — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and a carafe of local white wine (~€20-25)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to review your budget and see how much you have left for the final days. Fresh whole fish is sold by weight in Greece — ask the price before ordering to avoid surprises.

day_by_day.morning: Take one last leisurely morning swim in the Aegean Sea. Reflect on the trip and enjoy the warm water and beautiful scenery. Take photos and video to capture the memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack any souvenirs carefully and begin light packing. Take a final walk around the local area to revisit favorite spots — a café, a viewpoint, a beach cove. Grab a final Greek coffee and sit by the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Have a farewell dinner at your favorite taverna from the trip. Order dishes you loved most during the week. Chat with the owner or staff — Greek hospitality is legendary and these interactions are memorable.

meals.breakfast: Final big Greek breakfast at a seaside café — full spread with eggs, bread, honey, cheese, and coffee (~€7-9)
meals.lunch: One last gyros pita — a perfect budget farewell to Greek street food (~€3-4)
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite taverna of the trip — order your top dishes and enjoy a lingering final meal (~€13-16)

day_by_day.notes: Leave a genuine review for your favorite local restaurants and experiences — it helps small family businesses enormously. Begin sorting receipts and budgets for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take a final sunrise walk along the beach. Breathe in the sea air and take a last look at the Aegean. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort by the stated checkout time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport or port with plenty of time. Use public transport to keep costs low — local bus or shared taxi. At the airport, browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek products like mastiha liqueur or olive oil.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a full camera roll, and the taste of the Mediterranean still fresh. Begin planning your next Greek adventure on the flight home.

meals.breakfast: Quick and easy — Greek yogurt, fruit, and coffee from a nearby café or supermarket before checkout (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or use up any remaining supermarket snacks and provisions (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Keep travel documents, boarding passes, and passport easily accessible. Ensure all souvenirs comply with EU customs regulations for liquids and food products.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage and take a pre-arranged airport transfer or taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort facilities.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the resort bar or a nearby 24-hour souvlaki stand if available upon arrival. Budget around €8–12.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've had a long travel day. Hydrate well and get to bed early to start Day 2 refreshed. Confirm transfer arrangements before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time — water temperature is perfect for swimming this time of year.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's beachfront. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the immediate shoreline. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella if not included. Take a short walk to discover the nearest beach village or harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest local village for your first proper Greek dinner. Explore the main strip of tavernas and pick one with outdoor seating. Try classic Greek dishes to ease into the cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a Greek yogurt with honey and fresh fruit at a nearby café. Budget €8–14.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside snack bar — try a gyros wrap or a Greek salad with fresh bread. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna in the village — order grilled octopus, tzatziki, spanakopita, and a carafe of local house wine. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — this is your recovery and orientation day. Apply sunscreen generously; the Greek sun at 29°C is strong even with a sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim before the beach gets busy — the sea is calm and clear in the mornings. After swimming, visit a local morning market (laiki agora) if one operates nearby. Browse fresh produce, olives, local cheeses, and honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip or water taxi to a nearby secluded cove or hidden beach not accessible by road. Snorkel in the crystal-clear water and explore the rocky coastline. Most local operators offer 2–4 hour excursions at mid-range prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower, and head out for a sunset walk along the harbor promenade. Watch the fishing boats come in and chat with locals.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, local cheese (graviera or feta), and olives from the morning market. Eat on a bench by the sea. Budget €5–8.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat trip — pick up a tiropita (cheese pie) or koulouri from a local bakery. Budget €4–7.
meals.dinner: Harborfront seafood restaurant — order freshly caught grilled fish (ask what came in that day), with horta (wild greens) and lemon potatoes. Budget €22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat excursion the evening before or first thing in the morning as spots fill up quickly in June. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water for the boat trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic hilltop village (kastro). Explore on foot in the cooler morning hours before the heat peaks. Take in panoramic views of the Aegean and photograph the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a quieter, less-touristy beach recommended by locals — ask resort staff for their personal favorites. Spend the afternoon swimming and reading in a more peaceful setting. Try paddleboarding or kayaking if rentals are available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free open-air cultural event, local festival, or simply join the Greek evening promenade (volta) — a beloved local tradition of strolling through town after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a café near the archaeological site — Greek coffee (ellinikos) and a bougatsa (custard pastry). Budget €6–10.
meals.lunch: Simple taverna lunch near the beach — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad), stuffed tomatoes (gemista), and fresh lemonade. Budget €12–18.
meals.dinner: Mezze-style dinner at a local ouzerie — order 5–6 small plates to share: taramosalata, grilled sardines, saganaki (fried cheese), and ouzo or tsipouro. Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning archaeological or village visit. Carry water — temperatures peak around midday.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class or food tour focused on local Greek cuisine. Learn to make dishes like spanakopita, tzatziki, or fresh pasta with local herbs. Many resorts or nearby towns offer morning sessions lasting 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil producer or winery for a tasting session. Learn about Greek viticulture or olive cultivation and pick up a bottle or two to take home. Many estates offer guided tours at affordable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or recreate something you learned in the morning class using local ingredients, or enjoy dinner at a farm-to-table style restaurant that sources locally.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cooking class — a sesame koulouri and Greek coffee from a street vendor. Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Eat what you made in the cooking class — most sessions include a shared meal at the end. Budget typically included in class fee (€35–55 per person).
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table or garden restaurant with seasonal Greek menu — try lamb chops (paidakia), roasted vegetables, and local wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance. This is a great day to lean into your food interest — one of the highlights of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a neighboring island or coastal town by ferry or speedboat. Depart early to maximize time. Explore the town's old quarter, whitewashed alleys, and local churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the destination island's most famous beach. Grab lunch locally and explore a few more sights before the return ferry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel — you've had a full day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the ferry port café — a cheese pie and coffee. Budget €5–8.
meals.lunch: Local taverna on the day-trip island — try whatever the daily special is (mayirefta) for the most authentic and affordable meal. Budget €14–20.
meals.dinner: Low-key dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby neighborhood taverna. Try moussaka or pastitsio for a classic Greek comfort meal. Budget €18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance and book tickets online or at the port the day before. Bring a small daypack with sunscreen, swimwear, and a light layer for the boat ride.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time at the resort pool or beach. Read, journal, or simply enjoy doing nothing. This is your mid-trip recharge day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town on foot at a leisurely pace. Browse small shops selling local products — thyme honey, saffron, handmade ceramics, and local spirits. Visit a small local museum if one is nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a cliffside or rooftop bar with Aegean views. Watch the famous Greek sunset with an Aperol spritz or local wine before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — indulge in the spread. Budget included in stay or €12–18.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from local deli or bakery items — fresh bread, olives, cured meats, local cheeses. Eat by the harbor or beach. Budget €10–14.
meals.dinner: Romantic or atmospheric restaurant with a view — try grilled sea bream, calamari, and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The summer solstice falls on June 21 — enjoy the longest day of the year with a spectacular sunset. This is a perfect evening to splurge slightly on a special dining experience.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided snorkeling or diving excursion to explore underwater caves, reefs, or shipwrecks in the area. The warm, clear June water offers excellent visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the excursion, relax on a beach with beach bars and music — a more social and lively atmosphere for a change of pace. Try a frozen frappe or a cold Mythos beer.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local food and wine pairing evening or simply explore a different neighborhood of the main town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the excursion — eggs, fruit, and coffee. Budget included or €10–14.
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — club sandwich, Greek salad, and a cold drink. Budget €14–18.
meals.dinner: Neighborhood taverna away from the tourist strip — look for one where locals are eating. Try slow-cooked lamb kleftiko or stifado (beef stew). Budget €18–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling/diving excursions typically cost €40–80 per person depending on the operator and length. Book the day before. Bring anti-fog for goggles and reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter, ATV, or small car for the day to explore the island or coastal region independently. Drive to remote beaches, mountain villages, and viewpoints that public transport doesn't reach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover a hidden beach or cove found during your morning drive. Swim, snorkel, and have a completely private or uncrowded beach experience. Pack a picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Return the vehicle and wind down with a walk through a scenic village. Find a family-run taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast from a local bakery before picking up the rental — a spanakopita and Greek coffee. Budget €4–7.
meals.lunch: Picnic packed from a local supermarket or deli — olives, feta, bread, cherry tomatoes, and fruit. Eat at your hidden beach. Budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Family-run village taverna — try whatever the owner recommends. Often the most memorable and affordable meals come from these places. Budget €16–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Scooter/ATV rentals typically cost €25–45/day; small cars €40–65/day. Always wear a helmet and carry your passport for ID. Fill up on fuel before heading to remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fishing village early in the morning to watch the fishermen return with their catch. Chat with vendors at the small fish market. This is authentic Greece at its most unfiltered.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at one of the area's most scenic and well-regarded beaches. Arrive by midday to secure a good spot. Swim and unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live Greek music night (rebetiko or traditional folk music) at a local bar or cultural venue. Many venues host live music on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fish or seafood meze at the harbor — fried smelt or marinated anchovies with bread and wine if you're feeling adventurous. Budget €10–15.
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna — grilled shrimp, Greek salad, and tzatziki. Budget €16–22.
meals.dinner: Pre-music dinner at a casual restaurant — try souvlaki platter or a mixed grill with pita and sides. Budget €15–20 per person, plus drinks at the music venue.

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings or ask resort staff about live music nights happening this week. Greek evenings often don't start until 21:00 or later — embrace the late dining culture.

day_by_day.morning: Take a yoga or meditation session on the beach at sunrise (some resorts offer this) or simply do a peaceful solo walk along the shoreline. Reflect on the trip so far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Byzantine church, monastery, or historic chapel — often found on hilltops with stunning views. Light a candle and observe the quiet beauty of Greek Orthodox architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner for a special mid-trip celebration — pick a restaurant with a terrace, sea views, and a strong local wine list.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast or a smoothie bowl and coffee at a modern café. Budget €8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the monastery or church — a mezze plate, fresh juice, and coffee. Budget €10–14.
meals.dinner: Upscale taverna or seafood restaurant — try lobster pasta (astakomakaronada), grilled whole fish, and a bottle of local white wine. Budget €35–50 per person as a treat.

day_by_day.notes: When visiting churches or monasteries, dress modestly — shoulders and knees should be covered. Many provide wraps at the entrance. This is a wonderful cultural counterpoint to the beach days.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach of the trip for one last long swim. Soak up the sun and the Aegean views. Take photos and make mental memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the local town. Pick up gifts: local honey, olive oil, dried herbs, ceramic tiles, evil eye (mati) charms, or local liquors like mastiha or tsipouro.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best taverna you discovered during the trip. Order all your favorite dishes from the week and toast to a wonderful Greek holiday.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy every bite. Budget included or €12–18.
meals.lunch: Quick souvlaki or gyros from a street stand while shopping — the perfect casual Greek lunch. Budget €7–10.
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite restaurant of the trip — order generously and celebrate. Budget €25–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight so you're not rushed in the morning. Leave out only what you need for the morning of departure. Keep receipts for any duty-free purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beach or a last swim in the Aegean. Enjoy a slow final breakfast at the resort. Check out and arrange transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, explore any last spots near the airport or hotel area. Airport transfer and check-in procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with incredible memories of beaches, food, sunsets, and warm hospitality. Safe travels home.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at the resort — savor it. Budget included or €10–14.
meals.lunch: Airport café or a final souvlaki near the terminal. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Greek airports in peak summer season. Keep snacks and a water bottle handy for the journey home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and offer snorkeling opportunities in crystal-clear waters.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, and spices. Join a guided street food tour to sample spanakopita, loukoumades (honey donuts), souvlaki, and fresh Greek yogurt with honey. A true immersion into everyday Athenian food culture.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow lagoon-like waters. The unique color comes from crushed pink shells mixed with white sand. Wade through the warm shallow waters to reach the small island of Elafonissi and enjoy one of the most beautiful natural beaches in the Mediterranean.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink at the resort's bar.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and cocktails at the Aegean Bliss Resort's lounge bar upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort. Request early check-in preparation so your beachfront suite is perfectly ready. Luggage handling is handled by the concierge team.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start to your first full day. Take a slow stroll along the resort's private beachfront, breathing in the Aegean air. Enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon settling into paradise — lounge on the resort's private beach, take a dip in the warm Aegean Sea, and explore the resort's amenities including the infinity pool and spa. Book an introductory 60-minute Greek aromatherapy massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the resort's fine-dining restaurant for a curated 5-course Greek tasting menu featuring seasonal local ingredients, paired with selected Greek wines from Santorini and Nemea.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous buffet breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — fresh pastries, local honey, Greek yogurt, smoked salmon, and made-to-order eggs
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled octopus, tzatziki, spanakopita, and fresh-squeezed lemonade
meals.dinner: 5-course tasting menu at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant with Greek wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle orientation day — no rushing. Ask the concierge to brief you on upcoming excursions and make reservations for the rest of the trip. Confirm all island transfers and boat tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Athens city tour — explore the Acropolis and Parthenon with an expert archaeologist guide, bypassing standard queues with a premium fast-track ticket. Enjoy panoramic views of Athens from the Sacred Rock.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Central Market Food Tour: Dive into the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Taste local cheeses, cured meats, fresh olives, spices, and street food with a knowledgeable local food guide. Visit specialty delis and hidden tavernas that only locals know.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Athens restaurant in the Monastiraki or Kolonaki district, known for elevated modern Greek cuisine. Enjoy rooftop views of the illuminated Acropolis over a candlelit dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing for Athens
meals.lunch: Tastings and small plates throughout the Athens Central Market Food Tour — no separate lunch needed
meals.dinner: Upscale modern Greek restaurant in Athens — dishes like slow-braised lamb with kritharoto, sea bream carpaccio, and loukoumades with mastiha ice cream for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Athens is approximately 20–30 minutes from central areas by private transfer. Arrange a full-day private car and driver for comfort. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Acropolis and market tour. Book Acropolis fast-track tickets well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran or luxury yacht charter departing from the nearest marina. Sail to a secluded cove for morning swimming and snorkeling in crystal-clear Aegean waters. Enjoy fresh fruit, sparkling wine, and light bites on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private sailing experience, visiting a second hidden beach accessible only by boat. Swim, snorkel, and soak up the sun on the yacht's deck. The crew will prepare a gourmet onboard lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by sunset. Relax with sundowner cocktails at the beach bar watching the golden hour over the Aegean. Dinner at a local waterfront taverna in the nearest village, sampling the freshest catch of the day.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch prepared by the yacht crew — grilled fresh fish, Greek salad, hummus, pita, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood taverna — grilled whole sea bass, prawn saganaki, and fresh clams in white wine, paired with local white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book a private luxury catamaran or sailing yacht with a full crew including a skipper and chef. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. Departures are typically early to mid-morning for best sea conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning cooking class with a local Greek chef. Learn to make traditional dishes from scratch — spanakopita, moussaka, fresh tzatziki, and a classic Greek dessert like galaktoboureko. The class takes place in a charming local kitchen or villa setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil estate or winery for a premium tasting experience. Tour the groves or vineyards, learn about the production process, and taste award-winning extra virgin olive oils or indigenous Greek varietals like Assyrtiko and Agiorgitiko.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class — a sit-down dinner featuring the dishes you prepared, served with fine Greek wine in a beautiful setting. Alternatively, dine at the resort's restaurant with a personalized menu curated by the head chef.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with thyme honey and walnuts at the resort
meals.lunch: Tasting plates at the olive oil estate or winery — local cheeses, charcuterie, bread, and seasonal accompaniments
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the morning cooking class, served as a private dinner experience

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the cooking class and estate visit through the resort concierge. These experiences are typically intimate and private for premium guests. Bring a notebook — you'll want to recreate these recipes at home.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete (if accessible from your base, or by chartered flight/ferry). Arrive early to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoon before the crowds. Walk along the sandbar to the small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing at Elafonissi, one of Greece's most beautiful and unique beaches. The shallow warm waters and pink sand create an otherworldly atmosphere. Explore the surrounding dunes and natural landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at the resort, followed by a sunset cocktail at the beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch arranged by the resort — sandwiches, fresh fruit, local cheeses, sparkling water, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at the resort restaurant — fresh Cretan cuisine featuring dakos salad, slow-cooked lamb, and local cheeses

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi Beach is best visited early morning to avoid peak crowds. Arrange private transport or a chartered flight from your base for maximum comfort. The beach has limited facilities so the resort picnic is ideal. Wear water shoes as the lagoon has some rocky patches.

day_by_day.morning: Wellness morning at the resort spa — begin with a sunrise yoga session on the beachfront terrace, followed by a 90-minute couples or solo luxury spa treatment such as a hot stone massage or a traditional Greek herbal body wrap using local herbs and olive oil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided kayaking or paddleboarding experience along the coastline, exploring sea caves and hidden coves inaccessible by larger boats. A professional guide accompanies you for safety and local knowledge.
day_by_day.evening: Private beach dinner experience arranged by the resort — a candlelit table set directly on the sand with a personalized menu, dedicated waiter, and curated wine list. Watch the stars emerge over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Light wellness breakfast post-yoga — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Fresh salad and grilled protein at the resort beach club — tuna tataki, quinoa salad, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner — lobster thermidor, truffle risotto, and a decadent chocolate and mastiha dessert with Champagne

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner must be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. This is a perfect evening for a special occasion or romantic celebration. Bring a light wrap as sea breezes can be refreshing after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or ferry to Zakynthos (Zante) for the day. Check into a day-use suite at a luxury property or board a private boat directly. Begin with a visit to the famous Blue Caves on the northern tip of the island — stunning sea caves where the water glows brilliant blue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit — take a private boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed locations. The dramatic limestone cliffs, turquoise water, and the rusted shipwreck create an unforgettable scene. Swim in the enclosed bay and take in the views from the clifftop viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at a highly regarded restaurant in Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) before your return journey. Alternatively, return to the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Zakynthos — grilled calamari, fresh fish, and Greek salad with local white wine
meals.dinner: Traditional Zakynthian cuisine at a top-rated local restaurant — sofrito (veal in white wine sauce), bianco fish stew, and mandolato nougat for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat. Book a private boat charter for the most exclusive experience. The clifftop viewpoint above Navagio requires a short drive and walk but offers spectacular photo opportunities. Travel time from Athens area to Zakynthos is approximately 1 hour by domestic flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort. Enjoy a late breakfast and a final swim in the Aegean. Pack for an island-hopping interlude — take a private transfer to the port or airport for a short journey to Mykonos or Santorini for a 2-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini. Check into a luxury caldera-view cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli. Explore the iconic whitewashed village of Oia on foot — browse art galleries, designer boutiques, and artisan jewelry shops along the narrow cobblestone alleys.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing in Oia — one of the world's most celebrated sunsets. Secure a premium spot at a cliffside restaurant or bar well ahead of time. Watch the sun dip below the caldera in a blaze of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Oia upon arrival — fresh tomato fritters, fava dip, and local Santorinian wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a celebrated caldera-view restaurant in Oia — tasting menu featuring Santorinian specialties like white eggplant, cherry tomatoes, and fresh seafood paired with Assyrtiko wine

day_by_day.notes: Book your Santorini cave hotel well in advance — top properties sell out months ahead. Oia's sunset is extremely popular; arrive at your viewing spot at least 90 minutes early or book a restaurant with reserved sunset seating. Wear comfortable shoes for Oia's cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran tour of Santorini's caldera — sail past the volcanic islands of Nea Kameni and Palea Kameni. Hike up to the volcanic crater on Nea Kameni and swim in the warm thermal springs nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient ruins of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by a volcanic eruption, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private archaeologist guide for an in-depth experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Santorini at one of the island's most exclusive restaurants — an intimate setting carved into the caldera cliff with sweeping views of the volcanic archipelago, featuring the finest Greek cuisine and an exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Santorini hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, and Santorinian tomato jam with views of the caldera
meals.lunch: Onboard catamaran lunch — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and chilled Santorinian rosé
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course dinner at a top Santorini fine-dining restaurant — dishes like saffron-infused seafood risotto, grilled langoustine, and a volcanic lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. The catamaran tour typically includes snorkeling equipment, towels, and onboard catering. Evening temperatures in Santorini can be slightly cooler due to the altitude of Oia — bring a light jacket for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your base at the Aegean Bliss Resort via private transfer or short domestic flight. Spend the morning unwinding back at the resort, enjoying the familiar comfort of your beachfront suite. Optional: book a morning yoga or Pilates session at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local village or town nearest to the resort on foot or by private driver. Visit a local market, browse artisan shops for authentic Greek souvenirs — hand-painted ceramics, mastiha products, local olive oil, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a beloved local family-run taverna recommended by the resort — authentic home-style Greek cooking, generous hospitality, and a warm village atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast en route or upon arrival back at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local village café — traditional pastitsio, horiatiki salad, and fresh bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: Family-run taverna dinner — slow-roasted lamb, village sausages, grilled vegetables, and homemade baklava with local raki

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort concierge for their personal recommendation for the best local taverna — these hidden gems often serve the most authentic and memorable meals of any trip to Greece. Bring cash as many village establishments don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — make the most of the resort's private beachfront. Rent a luxury sun lounger cabana with dedicated service, order fresh juices and snacks, and spend the morning swimming in the warm Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury spa session — a 2-hour premium package including a hammam scrub, olive oil body massage, and facial treatment using local Greek botanical ingredients. Followed by time in the resort's heated pool.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — request a personalized menu from the head chef celebrating your 13-day journey through Greece. Toast with a bottle of premium Greek sparkling wine or Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full spread of Greek and continental favorites
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — fresh ceviche, grilled prawns, and a chilled Greek white wine
meals.dinner: Personalized farewell tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant — a celebration of the finest Greek flavors experienced throughout the trip, paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Inform the resort in advance that this is your last evening — many luxury properties will arrange special touches such as room decoration, a personalized menu card, or a complimentary dessert to mark the occasion. Begin packing this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last breakfast at the resort overlooking the Aegean Sea. Take a slow walk along the beach, collect a few shells, and soak in the views one final time. Complete any last-minute packing and souvenir organization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. The concierge will arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Depending on your departure time, stop at a nearby café or market for a final Greek coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with extraordinary memories of 13 days of luxury beaches, world-class food, ancient history, and Aegean magic.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely breakfast at the resort — Greek coffee, fresh orange juice, tiropita, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a café near the airport — Greek mezze platter and sparkling water
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport check-in, especially during the busy summer season. The resort concierge can arrange duty-free shopping assistance and ensure your luggage is transported seamlessly. Consider purchasing local olive oil, mastiha liqueur, and Greek honey as premium gifts to take home.
